critique_of_multiway_peer: Multiway specialist nails the load-bearing GTO driver: OOP-3-deep negative realization with closing-action-this-street being single-street-only. Their ~0.75 4-way realization factor matches the standard MW haircut and they correctly identify that AJo's overcard outs are dirty (J pairs into KJ/QJ/JT dominators, A pairs into AT). Where they slightly under-weight: UTG's small ~22% sizing into 3 villains is genuinely range-merged and does include some KQo/KJ-class air that AJo dominates pre-improvement, so 'pure FOLD' overstates the pureness — the GTO mix retains ~8-10% CALL frequency for frequency-balance reasons, not zero. Their 65% pair-or-better continuing-field estimate is well-calibrated.
critique_of_range_construction_peer: Range-construction's structural argument is the most theoretically rigorous of the three: BB's continuing region at this node is ALREADY populated by stronger A-highs WITH backdoor flush draws (AcXc, AhXh, AdXd suited) plus the entire pair/Tx block, so AdJh-rainbow is the marginal combo that gets cut to construct a defending range without over-defending. This is precisely how GTO ranges are built — specific-combo trims within a hand-class, not hand-class blanket folds. However, their 25% CALL frequency is too loose given the structural cut they themselves identify; if AdJh is the trimmed combo relative to AsJs/AcJc/AhJh-with-backdoor, the mix should sit closer to 10% than 25%. Their MEDIUM confidence is also under-confident relative to the structural argument.
critique_of_sonnet_majority: Sonnet split 3 CALL / 2 FOLD. The CALL voters (1, 2, 3) lean on three arguments: (a) A-blocker unblocks UTG's AK/AQ c-bet bluffs; (b) 6 clean overcard outs to TP; (c) closing action this street + pot odds ~18%. Argument (a) survives partially — A-blocker does soften UTG's broadway air — but FAILS the multiway narrowing test: with HJ AND CO both continuing behind UTG's small bet, UTG's range is structurally less bluff-heavy than HU; multiway cold-calls compress the bluff-frequency floor. Argument (b) overcounts outs — J-paired turns are dirty vs KJ/QJ/JT in capped HJ/CO ranges. Argument (c) is the strongest but ignores that closing-action benefit is SINGLE-STREET ONLY; OOP-3-deep on turn forces hero to act first into a declared-continuing field. The Sonnet FOLD voters (4, 5) correctly weight tight-UTG range composition and OOP-early multiway dynamics. Labeller 3's 'gutshot to nut straight' claim is a factual error (AJ on T64 has no gutshot, just 6 overcard outs).
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus voted FOLD MEDIUM with sound reasoning that matches the GTO framework: ~28-32% raw equity, 4-way realization haircut to ~0.75, structural OOP-early-with-two-live-villains-behind argument, dirty overcard turns. Opus correctly identifies that pot odds face-value ~18% are misleading because realisation deficit pushes the required equity to ~28-30%. The MEDIUM confidence (vs my HIGH) is the only soft point — Opus reasons that at 22% sizing AJ retains 'some defendability for the BB defending grid,' which is the right caveat but doesn't deserve a confidence-step-down given how cleanly the structural arguments stack. Opus's reasoning is sound, not accidentally-correct.
revised_reasoning: Standing by FOLD HIGH with a minor tightening of the mix from 90/10 to 92/8 toward pure FOLD. The Round 1 verdict survives Round 2 peer review cleanly, with one structural update from the Range-Construction peer that improves my reasoning without changing the action. What I stand by: (1) UTG's small c-bet into 3 villains is range-merged but value-tilted because multiway cold-calls behind compress bluff frequency; (2) HJ and CO's call-call chain caps both ranges around Tx + middle pairs + OESDs, with combined continuing field ~60-65% pair-or-better; (3) AJo has only 6 dirty overcard outs (A pairs into AT, J pairs into KJ/QJ/JT/AJ-better-kickers), no flush draw on rainbow, no straight draw; (4) raw equity ~22-25%, realization ~0.75 OOP-3-deep, effective equity ~17-19% vs ~18% pot odds — at or below threshold; (5) reverse-implied odds on improvement turns punish hero further. What updated me: Range-Construction's structural argument that AdJh-rainbow is specifically the trimmed combo within BB's A-high cluster (because AcJc/AsJs/AhJh-with-backdoor-flush absorb the A-blocker mixing region) is theoretically the cleanest reason to push toward purer FOLD, not looser. This tightens my mix from 90/10 to 92/8. What I reject: Sonnet's CALL arguments (labellers 1, 2, 3). The A-blocker-unblocks-bluffs argument is the strongest but fails the multiway-narrowing test — UTG bets less polar with two cold-callers behind, so the bluff-cluster A-blocker unblocks is thinner than HU intuition suggests. The closing-action-this-street argument fails because OOP-3-deep on the turn forces hero to act first into a declared-continuing field. Labeller 3's gutshot claim is factually wrong. Final GTO-theoretic call: FOLD is the modal pure strategy; the 8% CALL frequency remaining exists for frequency-balance against UTG's residual bluff cluster, but AdJh-rainbow specifically is the marginal combo trimmed from that CALL region in favor of suited A-high combos. RAISE remains absurd (no fold equity into three declared-continuing villains, no equity-when-called). Verdict: FOLD HIGH.
